_about: References cited by the impact assessment (knowledge/impact/settings.json, farmponds.json and the atlas's Impact assessment tab). Each entry: id, short (how it is cited in text), citation, url (a public copy where one exists), doi where known, and what it is used for.

references.citation: Singh T, Gujar S, Kaur R, Seth A (2026). Use of satellite data for impact assessment of desilting interventions in waterbodies. Manuscript, IIT Delhi and Plaksha University.
references.used_for: Desilting: matching each desilted waterbody with similar untreated waterbodies, rainfall-matched before and after years, and difference-in-differences on how long water lasts; heterogeneity by rainfall zone and size.

references.citation: Kaur R (2026). Validating impact: field observations from waterbody rejuvenation in Madhya Pradesh. CoRE Stack blog.
references.used_for: Desilting: field checks of the satellite-based impact estimates in Chhatarpur district.

references.citation: Kaur R, Bansal K, Garg D, Sardana R, Vishnubhatla S, Agrawal S, Kumari S, Singla P, Seth A (2024). Assessing the impact of farm ponds on agricultural productivity in Northern India. ACM SIGCAS/SIGCHI Conference on Computing and Sustainable Societies (COMPASS '24), New Delhi.
references.used_for: Farm ponds: treated sites and matched control sites without ponds, difference-in-differences on vegetation around the pond for up to five years, effects in drought years and on drought sensitivity, by season.

references.citation: Borusyak K, Jaravel X, Spiess J (2024). Revisiting event-study designs: robust and efficient estimation. Review of Economic Studies 91(6): 3253-3285.
references.used_for: Farm ponds, headline: the imputation estimator for staggered adoption (fit unit and time effects on untreated observations, impute the untreated outcome of treated observations).

references.citation: Callaway B, Sant'Anna PHC (2021). Difference-in-differences with multiple time periods. Journal of Econometrics 225(2): 200-230.
references.used_for: Farm ponds: cohort-by-year effects with not-yet-treated controls, and why a single two-way fixed-effects regression is avoided when ponds are built in different years.

references.citation: Sant'Anna PHC, Zhao J (2020). Doubly robust difference-in-differences estimators. Journal of Econometrics 219(1): 101-122.
references.used_for: Farm ponds, robustness: doubly robust DiD (propensity score and outcome regression) within each district.

references.citation: Chernozhukov V, Demirer M, Duflo E, Fernández-Val I (2018, revised 2025). Generic machine learning inference on heterogeneous treatment effects in randomized experiments. NBER Working Paper 24678.
references.used_for: Farm ponds, heterogeneity: best linear predictor (BLP), sorted group average effects (GATES) and classification analysis (CLAN) on cross-fitted machine-learning predictions.

references.citation: Wager S, Athey S (2018). Estimation and inference of heterogeneous treatment effects using random forests. Journal of the American Statistical Association 113(523): 1228-1242.
references.used_for: Farm ponds, heterogeneity: forests for treatment-effect variation.

references.citation: Abadie A, Diamond A, Hainmueller J (2010). Synthetic control methods for comparative case studies: estimating the effect of California's tobacco control program. Journal of the American Statistical Association 105(490): 493-505.
references.used_for: Desilting: the counterfactual model (a treated waterbody fitted on its controls over the pre years and projected over the post years), and placebo-based inference: placing an estimate among the same estimates for untreated units.

references.citation: Stuart EA (2010). Matching methods for causal inference: a review and a look forward. Statistical Science 25(1): 1-21.
references.used_for: Desilting: nearest-neighbour matching of controls on covariates (Mahalanobis distance) and balance.

references.citation: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (2016, updated 2020). Manual for Drought Management. Government of India.
references.used_for: Drought years: the 3-4 week dry-spell trigger behind 4 or more weeks of moderate or severe kharif drought.

references.citation: CoRE Stack: Commoning for Resilience and Equity. Surface water body, zone-of-influence, cropping intensity and drought layers.
references.used_for: All data: seasonal water extent of each waterbody per hydrological year, the zone of influence and its cropping, MWS cropping and kharif drought weeks.
